| [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) v4 | In a Hilbert-space model only unitarily invariant structure is intrinsic; a basis or tensor factorisation, and so any parts or features, is extra data supplied from outside the space, and the record's Hilbert-space works differ in where they get it | Carroll (2021), [LIT-123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md): a quantum theory is fixed up to unitary equivalence by the Hamiltonian's spectrum, and subsystems come from a factorisation that the dynamics must select. Van Rijsbergen ([LIT-262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)) computes only traces and inner products, and treats each observable's eigenbasis as a "point of view". DisCoCat's ε/η composition ([LIT-273](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md)) is orthogonally covariant, while its Frobenius sequel ([LIT-272](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)) stipulates a basis and composes by elementwise product in it. [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) is the same point for learned representations. This is a synthesis across the four, not a result any one of them states. It does not say that basis-dependent models are wrong; it says what they have assumed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-020.md) | Every Boolean algebra is the clopen algebra of its Stone space of prime ideals, and a finite one is the power set of its atoms, so a single Boolean context always has two-valued valuations and the Kochen–Specker obstruction lies in how contexts overlap | Stone (1936, 1937), [LIT-353](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md) and [LIT-358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-358.md): every Boolean ring is isomorphic to the compact open sets of its prime-ideal space, a totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff space that is compact exactly when there is a unit, and every such space arises this way. Kochen & Specker ([LIT-298](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-298.md), Thm 0) turn this into the criterion that a partial Boolean algebra embeds in a Boolean one iff its two-valued homomorphisms separate points. The joining of the two, that non-classicality needs more than one context, is the record's. Neither Stone paper uses "ultrafilter" or states a duality of categories. | Active |
| [THEORY-021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-021.md) v2 | In the exact configurations of uniform superposition (regular polygons, the tetrahedron, antipodal pairs, and tegum products of these that span the hidden space, with equal norms within each factor) the features form a rank-one POVM compressed from the n-feature basis: their dimensionality-weighted projectors sum to the identity | Elhage et al. (2022), [LIT-323](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-323.md), found that features in uniform superposition settle into polytopes and tegum products, with feature dimensionalities clustering at 3/4, 2/3, 1/2, 2/5 and 3/8. It does not make superposition contextual or quantum, and it says nothing yet about trained real models. | Active |
| [THEORY-024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md) v2 | Classical Boolean logic is restored when a presheaf of contextual data acquires a global section or is sheafified | Ghose (2025), [LIT-276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md) — asserts that the Heyting algebra of truth values "becomes Boolean" when the presheaf data collapse to a global section, and that sheaves encode Boolean reasoning. Both claims are asserted, not proved. The record's readings refute them. The internal logic of a topos is fixed by the base category and its topology, not by whether one presheaf has a section (Isham–Butterfield, [LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md), §6). Sheaf toposes such as Sh(ℝ) are not Boolean ([NOTE-249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md)). The contextuality criterion itself is untouched. | Rejected |
| [THEORY-037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md) v3 | In the topos programme quantum propositions form a distributive Heyting algebra, not an orthocomplemented lattice, and its negation is a pseudo-complement under which excluded middle can fail | Döring & Isham (2007, II), [LIT-335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md) — daseinisation maps each projector injectively to a clopen sub-object of the spectral presheaf, with δ(P∨Q) = δ(P)∨δ(Q) but only δ(P∧Q) ⪯ δ(P)∧δ(Q). | [THEORY-041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-041.md) | Birkhoff and von Neumann proposed the modular law, not orthomodularity, and proved it fails for closed subspaces in infinite dimension; Husimi used the orthomodular identity only as an unnamed proof step | Birkhoff & von Neumann (1936), [LIT-306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md) — the lattice of closed subspaces is orthocomplemented and not distributive. They propose modularity (L5), motivated by a dimension function, and give an explicit infinite-dimensional pentagon that breaks it. The word "orthomodular" does not occur. Husimi (1937), [LIT-357](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-357.md), derives modularity as the parallelogram law under a finite-chain assumption and uses the orthomodular identity as a step without naming it. Citing either paper for "the orthomodular lattice of quantum logic" misattributes it. | Active |
| [THEORY-042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-042.md) | Under a superselection rule a coherent superposition across sectors is operationally a mixture, because no observable connects the sectors; Wick, Wightman and Wigner proved such a rule for integer versus half-integer spin and only postulated it for charge | Wick, Wightman & Wigner (1952), [LIT-339](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-339.md) — they define a superselection rule and show that a superposition across sectors "is not a pure state, but a statistical mixture". They prove the rule from time reversal for integer versus half-integer angular momentum, and postulate it for charge with "no conclusive evidence". What follows for Birkhoff–von Neumann's lattice ([LIT-306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md)), a product of sector lattices with central sector projections, is the record's inference. The centre-of-the-algebra formulation belongs to Haag, who is not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-160.md) v2 | In the algebraic Hamiltonian setting, symmetry and conservation correspond because the bracket is antisymmetric, which for a bilinear bracket is each observable conserving itself; the theorem's content lies in identifying observables with generators | Baez (2020), [LIT-819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-819.md), read in [NOTE-630](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-630.md), Theorems 3, 4, 8 and 10, with Alfsen and Shultz's theorem quoted as Theorem 12 and not checked here (QUESTION-142). With unique solutions to the flow equations, "a generates symmetries of b iff b generates symmetries of a" is {a, b} = 0 ⇔ {b, a} = 0. It assumes reversible one-parameter groups and an observable–generator map; it says nothing about dissipative or stochastic dynamics, nor about the Lagrangian form of Noether's theorem. | Active |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v3 | When the causal constraints on events depend on context, deterministic assignments that are causal in each context can fail to glue into one causal assignment, so causal structure is itself a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). Over a space of input histories with the lowerset topology, causal functions form a separated presheaf, and on the space Θ₃ it is not a sheaf: two causal assignments on disjoint opens give one event two outputs on their common extension. That example was checked here, and it settles the claim. The source's Theorem 2.34, that the presheaf is a sheaf exactly when no two contexts impose incompatible causal pasts on a common event, is reported as the source's. Its proof was not read, and it is QUESTION-143. It does not say any physical or quantum data display the effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) v2 | Classical simulations between empirical models on different scenarios never create contextuality, and a map between model sets is such a simulation exactly when a non-contextual model of the hom scenario induces it | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md); Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2021, v2 2024), [LIT-845](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-845.md). No-signalling models only, and nothing about information preserved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md) v3 | Within classical realism, a generalized-noncontextuality no-go refutes Leibnizian representations, not realist representations as such; it rests on a stronger assumption than a Bell-like no-go and so applies where none exists, as in prepare-measure scenarios, but only Leibnizianity implying noncontextuality is proved | Schmid, Selby and Spekkens (2020), [LIT-945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-945.md), §VI.C, §VIII (Eqs. 200, 214, 215), read in part in [NOTE-737](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-737.md), which is Skimmed: §§II–IV and the proofs in Appendices C–G were not read. The converse is Conjecture 1′, so a Leibnizianity failure is not shown to be a noncontextuality failure. The prepare-measure claim is stated, not derived, in the text read. | Active |
| [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md) v3 | In Aerts's subspace model of Hampton's membership data, and in any lattice whose membership weight is order-preserving, whatever its negation, taking concept conjunction and disjunction as meet and join cannot produce overextension or underextension, so a model of the guppy-type deviations must take conjunction as some operation other than the meet or drop the monotone weight, while the Kolmogorov-type deviations can be had from the meet of a non-Boolean subspace lattice | Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), Theorem 9 and §§2.2–3.3, read in full in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md). The fits that place the k-type deviations in a tilted subspace lattice and the ∆-type ones in an emergent sector are models with free parameters, not tests. | [THEORY-309](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-309.md) v2 | If contexts are defined by joint measurability alone, every nondisturbing correlation, maximally contextual ones included, is realized by trivial measurements on a one-dimensional quantum system, so Kochen–Specker contextuality needs a stronger operational notion of context | Budroni, Cabello, Gühne, Kleinmann & Larsson (2022), [LIT-263](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-263.md), §IV.B.2, Eqs. 27–28, adapting Fritz (2012), read in [NOTE-844](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-844.md). Liang, Spekkens & Wiseman's sharpness parameter is the other known escape. | Active |
| [THEORY-315](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-315.md) v2 | For a state whose four-state reflection orbit is realizable, generalized noncontextuality bounds two binary predictabilities by \|⟨X⟩\| + \|⟨Z⟩\| ≤ 1, so the form of a predictability trade-off, not its existence, can witness contextuality | Catani, Leifer, Scala, Schmid and Spekkens (2022), [LIT-980](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-980.md), read in [NOTE-825](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-825.md). Proved analytically, with a saturating model, for preparation noncontextuality and exact operational equivalence. The bound constrains a whole uncertainty relation only in a theory where every state has the orbit; the qubit's circle violates it, and a classical theory without the symmetry escapes it. It needs no perfectly distinguishable states, and it is not a sheaf or Kochen–Specker criterion. | Active |
| [THEORY-403](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-403.md) | The single-photon Mach–Zehnder phenomenology with balanced beamsplitters and phases 0 or π, including which-way detection, the bomb tester, delayed choice and the quantum eraser, is reproduced exactly by a local, deterministic classical field model with an epistemic restriction, so that slice of interference forces neither complementarity, nor observer-dependent reality, nor nonlocality | Catani, Leifer, Schmid & Spekkens (2021), [LIT-019](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-019.md), read in full in [NOTE-018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-018.md). | [THEORY-416](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-416.md) | Quantum thermodynamics has at least four inequivalent notions of work, the ensemble average, the two-point-measurement random variable, the ε-deterministic single-shot work content and the resource-theory work, which answer different operational questions; only the two single-shot optima coincide, by identification of formulas and for energy-diagonal states | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md). Only the last two agree, and that agreement is an observation that two published formulas match, for states diagonal in energy. It is an informed judgement of a 2016 snapshot, not a theorem that the notions cannot be unified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-455](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-455.md) | Every finite stochastic transition matrix on a configuration space equals the entrywise squared modulus of a complex matrix, unitary after dilation, so the Hilbert-space formalism can be written over any indivisible stochastic process as a non-unique representation; within that representation interference is the term by which the process fails to divide at an intermediate time, relative to the chosen configurations, and an ideal correlating environment restores divisibility | Barandes (2023), [LIT-086](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-086.md), read in full in [NOTE-080](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-080.md). Interference is the cross-term of Eq. 43 against a would-be Markov factorization, and a perfectly correlating environment that then evolves separately makes the process divisible (Eqs. 45–56). The "emergent" Schrödinger equation is the definition of H, unitarity is a choice the claimed gauge freedom does not preserve, and the decomposition is relative to a configuration basis the paper never fixes. | Active |
| [THEORY-459](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-459.md) | Exact duality between two models is incompatible with ontological emergence of one from the other, reductive or not, because a duality is an isomorphism and ontological emergence needs a non-injective linkage whose interpretation does not commute; the two combine only when emergence runs beside the duality, as along the radial direction in AdS/CFT, through an approximate duality, or as merely epistemic emergence | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), §14.3, read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). | [THEORY-474](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-474.md) | Spekkens' toy bit theory, restricted to maximal knowledge and post-selected measurements, has a universal, sound and complete ZX-style graphical calculus whose phase-free rules and symplectic check-matrix conditions are exactly those of pure qubit stabilizer theory; the two calculi differ in the phase group, the Klein four-group against Z₄ | Backens & Duman (2014), [LIT-054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-054.md), read in full in [NOTE-066](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-066.md). | [THEORY-479](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-479.md) | Shannon's chain rule is the 1-cocycle equation of a cohomology of finite probability spaces whose action is averaged conditioning, and on connected, sufficiently rich structures of partitions every measurable 1-cocycle is a constant multiple of Shannon entropy, with no symmetry or continuity axiom assumed; in the unitary-invariant quantum version the first cohomology vanishes and von Neumann entropy is the 0-cochain whose coboundary is minus Shannon entropy | Baudot & Bennequin (2015), [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md), read in [NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md). | [THEORY-482](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-482.md) | For a closed quantum system that starts thermal and is measured projectively in energy before and after a unitary drive, the two-point-measurement work obeys the Jarzynski equality and the Tasaki–Crooks relation in exactly the classical form, because those energy measurements erase the coherences in which a quantum difference could appear | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md), which reproduces the derivation (Eqs. 24–30). The identity is exact under its conditions. Its classicality is bought by the definition of work: two projective energy measurements destroy coherences, which is why the definition is contested. It says nothing about work defined without them. | Active |
| [THEORY-485](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-485.md) | Wave-function realism falsifies causal closure restricted to spacetime but is compatible with closure relative to fundamental physics, so quantum ontology opens no causal gap for non-physical causes; what it forces on the physicalist is a criterion of the physical and a bridge from dynamical to causal completeness | Poltorak (2026), [LIT-164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md), an unrefereed preprint read in full in [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md). "Every physical effect has a sufficient physical cause" has two tacit parameters, a domain and a completeness relation. With the domain set to spacetime the principle fails under wave-function realism; with it set to the ontology of a complete fundamental theory it survives. The move to a breach needs a premise that wave-function realists deny. The conclusions are modest and close to analytic once the terms are defined. The target is conceded to be a picture, not a published argument, and the dynamical-to-causal bridge is asserted, not argued. | Proposed |

Unpublished as of the reading. | Active |
| [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) | For any presheaf of propositions over a small category of contexts, a sieve-valued valuation satisfies the generalized functional-composition condition exactly when it is a subobject of that presheaf, and the construction runs unchanged in classical physics, where every microstate gives a global section yet truth values are still non-Boolean sieves; so the logic of the truth values is fixed by the base category, not by whether a presheaf has global sections | Butterfield & Isham (1998), [LIT-381](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-381.md), read in full in [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md): Theorem 4.1 proves that generalized FUNC is exactly naturality of ν : G → Ω, for any presheaf G of posets on any small category. In classical physics the value presheaf has a global section per microstate (3.6–3.7), yet the macrostate and microstate valuations are sieve-valued, and [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md) shows excluded middle failing at a microstate. Isham & Butterfield (1999), [LIT-389](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md) ([NOTE-334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-334.md)), adds that Ω is unique for a given topos and that a base with one arrow between any two objects gives two-valued logic. The choice of base, and so of the logic, remains free. | Active |
| [THEORY-524](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-524.md) | On cyclic measurement scenarios, where the contexts' overlaps form one chordless N-cycle, the ℤ/2 Čech obstruction computed on the (N−1)-th iterated joint model is exact for logical and strong contextuality, the bound N − 1 being tight; beyond cycles no such result is established, the published extension is false on its own example, and the completeness conjecture fails on a Kochen–Specker cover that is never detected at any level | Carù (2018), [LIT-280](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-280.md), read in [NOTE-253](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-253.md), and the same result republished as Thm IV.32 of Carù's 2019 thesis, [LIT-281](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-281.md), read in [NOTE-254](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-254.md). The cyclic theorem is proved and was confirmed on Hardy, on the (2,2,4) counterexample and on 659 random contextual cycle models. The failures beyond cycles (Prop 8.2 / IV.34, the §8 cover, Conjecture 9.1 / IV.41) are the readers' computations and a lifting lemma, not the author's. The joint models grow exponentially; nothing analyses the cost. | Active |
| [THEORY-526](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-526.md) | The Čech cohomology obstruction of a support section is a sound but incomplete witness of contextuality: it vanishes exactly when the section lies in a compatible family of integer combinations of support sections, so it is non-zero on every section of every All-vs-Nothing model, over any coefficient ring, on a connected cover, yet it misses the Hardy model entirely, part of a strongly contextual Kochen–Specker cover, and every section of a strongly contextual model on the fully symmetric (2,2,4) Bell cover | Abramsky, Mansfield & Barbosa (2011), [LIT-277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md) ([NOTE-250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-250.md)); Abramsky, Barbosa, Kishida, Lal & Mansfield (2015), [LIT-278](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-278.md) ([NOTE-251](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-251.md)); Carù (2017), [LIT-279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-279.md) ([NOTE-252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-252.md)). The criterion (Prop 4.2 / Prop 16) and the All-vs-Nothing theorem (Thm 21) are proved; the three failures are explicit models, which the readers re-computed exactly over ℤ and ℤ/2. Two steps are the readers': that the §8 cover and the (2,2,4) model admit no All-vs-Nothing argument over any ring, by Thm 21 read contrapositively. The witness is possibilistic, so it cannot grade anything below strong contextuality. | Active |
| [THEORY-535](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-535.md) | Quantum systems read as bundles of property-instances with no principle of individuality can have their kinds and their number stated in quasi-set theory, so that N indistinguishable particles get a definite quasi-cardinal without labels; the construction covers kinds and counting only, not states, actualization or dynamics | Holik, Jorge, Krause & Lombardi (2021), [LIT-107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md), read in full from the preprint in [NOTE-127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-127.md). The Lombardi–da Costa ontology of properties makes a quantum system a bundle of instances of universal type-properties, with no principle of individuality. Krause's quasi-set theory Q, reinterpreted over property-instances, represents an atomic bundle as a qset taking one instance from each qset of indiscernibles, guaranteed by Q's Axiom of Choice, and N particles as a subqset of quasi-cardinal N. The new formal content is about two pages (§6), the printed proofs contain errors, and states, actualization and dynamics are not formalized. The claims about Kochen–Specker and non-separability are recharacterizations by definition, not results. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-545](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-545.md) | Aerts and Gabora's founding quantum model of concepts is a classical probability model written in a Hilbert space: every context it uses is a projector diagonal in one basis, so the contexts commute and generate a Boolean algebra, its entangled 'pet fish' state gives the same statistics as a classically correlated mixture for every context in the model, and its guppy weights are copied from single-concept ratings rather than predicted for the conjunction | Aerts & Gabora (2005), Parts II and I, [LIT-312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-312.md) and [LIT-340](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-340.md), read in [NOTE-299](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-299.md) and [NOTE-294](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-294.md). The structural facts are checks of the published model, not of the authors' prose: contexts are sums of basis projectors, counts are chosen to match rounded frequencies, and the authors call the result a "quantization" of a set-theoretical model. Part I's mark of non-classicality (eq. 19) is met by Boolean projection lattices too, and its lattice structure is supposed, not derived. The model as printed is also infeasible in two cells. It does not say that no quantum model of concepts does better. | Active |
| [THEORY-553](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-553.md) | In the Döring–Isham topos representation of quantum theory a bounded physical quantity cannot take values in the topos's real-number object; it is represented faithfully by an arrow from the spectral presheaf to a presheaf of monotone real functions over subcontexts, so its value at a context is a spread that widens as the context shrinks, and these values form only a commutative monoid, under which sums of daseinised quantities are not daseinisations of sums | Döring & Isham, paper III (2007/8), [LIT-299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-299.md) ([NOTE-290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-290.md)), restated with additions in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). The Gel'fand transforms of daseinised operators grow as contexts shrink, so arrows into the constant presheaf ℝ are impossible (3.3–3.4). Each Â gives a natural transformation δ̆^o(A) : Σ → ℝ^⪰ (Thm 3.1), and Â ↦ δ̆^o(A) is injective, by de Groote's results. ℝ^⪰ is a monoid, not a group; differences need a group completion, whose global elements are the functions of bounded variation on the context poset. No choice among the candidate value objects is made, and the state-dependent reading of the spread is cited, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md) | In Kolmogorovian probability, joint distributedness is transitive, so representing a measurement by one random variable in every context it occurs in already puts all measurements of a connected system on one probability space; within that representation a Kochen–Specker or Bell contradiction refutes the context-independent identification of measurements, not the existence of a joint distribution | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-836.md), read in full in [NOTE-623](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-623.md). The transitivity step is an elementary proof; the reading of the reductio is an argument that rests on it. It binds the random-variable representation only: the sheaf account keeps one variable per measurement and asks whether marginals glue, and a reader who holds that view is not bound by it. The paper also proves that a coupling of a binary connection is multimaximal iff adjacent pairs, ordered by their means, are maximally coupled (Theorem II.3). | Active |
| [THEORY-580](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-580.md) v2 | On any cover of a space of input histories, the empirical models compatible with a causal structure are exactly the points of a polytope cut from a product of simplices by linear causality equations, so how much of a model a causal structure can explain is a linear program; causal separability is relative to an assumed ambient structure, and the causally separable fraction is never less than the separable local fraction | Gogioso and Pinzani (2023), [LIT-788](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-788.md), skimmed in [NOTE-624](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-624.md), with the proofs of the causaltope theorems (2.18, 2.19, 2.25) and of the lower bound (2.29) read and checked on promotion (2026-10-20), against the definitions they take from The Topology of Causality. The proofs are short because the work is in the definitions; the one step left implicit closes. The quantum switches witness indefinite order only relative to an ambient space with known no-signalling constraints, not absolutely. | Active |
| [THEORY-584](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-584.md) | The quantum fidelity tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) is exactly the classical Bhattacharyya overlap of the two states' outcome distributions minimized over all measurements, and the minimum is attained by a projective measurement whose eigenvalues are square roots of likelihood ratios | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md). min over POVMs of Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) equals tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28), attained in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67), whose eigenvalues are √(tr ρ0E_b / tr ρ1E_b) (Eq. 3.92). Proved for invertible ρ1 with a separate support construction, in finite dimension. The fidelity is the unsquared one; Jozsa's is its square. The thesis says nothing about trace distance, and the analogous problems for Rényi overlaps and the quantum Chernoff bound are left open. | Active |
| [THEORY-585](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-585.md) v2 | In the Döring–Isham scheme for realising collections of systems in topoi, disjoint sums of quantum systems compose exactly; along a tensor product of finite-dimensional systems, the pull-back of a constituent's quantity agrees with the composite's own quantity at a context exactly when every projection in it with proper support on the first factor has the form P⊗1, so it fails for every non-scalar quantity and no operator on the composite realises the pull-back | Döring & Isham, paper IV (2007/8), [LIT-310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-310.md) ([NOTE-285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-285.md)), restated in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) §§11–13 ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). Classical physics satisfies the translation condition (3.18) exactly. For quantum disjoint sums the pull-back of δ̆(A₁⊕A₂) is δ̆(A₁) (Lemma 4.2, 4.24; checked). For H₁⊗H₂ the pull-back gives δ(Â₁)_{V_W}⊗1̂ at each context W, which equals δ(Â₁⊗1̂)_W on contexts V₁⊗ℂ1̂. That it differs elsewhere, and that no operator realises it, are asserted. The rules are "partly experimental", and the trivial-system rule contradicts the series' own definition of contexts. | Active |
| [THEORY-586](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-586.md) | The ψ-ontology theorems exclude only overlap of the distributions that distinct quantum states induce over ontic states; overlap is sufficient but not necessary for reading ψ as knowledge, so a model in which the state is ψ-ontic in Harrigan and Spekkens' sense can still have ψ represent partial knowledge | Hance, Rarity & Ladyman (2021), [LIT-090](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-090.md), read in full in [NOTE-072](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-072.md). The formal ψ-ontic/ψ-epistemic split is contradictory by stipulation, while the informal "ontic" and "epistemic" are not exclusive. So PBR and the related theorems bound the geometry of µ_ψ, not the interpretation of ψ. The paper proves nothing; its positive criterion (Eq. 6) is predictive incompleteness, and its Appendix A makes claims the record's readings contradict. The defensible paraphrase of PBR is "not ψ-epistemic in the overlap sense, given preparation independence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-592](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-592.md) | Every unital Banach *-algebra satisfying Gelfand and Naimark's norm conditions is isometrically *-isomorphic to a norm-closed algebra of operators on a Hilbert space, built from positive functionals by what is now the GNS construction, and a commutative one is the algebra of all continuous functions on its compact maximal-ideal space | Gelfand & Naimark (1943), [LIT-313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-313.md), read in full in [NOTE-303](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-303.md). Theorem 1 embeds every normed *-ring in B(H) for a Hilbert space not assumed separable; Lemma 1 is the commutative case, resting on Gelfand's 1941 paper and Šilov's boundary. The paper never says "C*-algebra" or "GNS". It assumes two axioms it suspected redundant, and notes that a single norm identity may replace two others. It gives the object-level isomorphism R ≅ C(𝔐), not a categorical duality, and nothing on uniqueness or irreducibility of the representation. | Active |
| [THEORY-594](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-594.md) | Unitarily inequivalent representations in quantum field theory need not refute ontic structural realism: what does physical work in spontaneous symmetry breaking and in the DHR derivation of quantum statistics is structure across representations, so a structural realist who takes structure to be modal and to span them can accept that work, though the modal conception is undeveloped and the removal of Howard's premise rests on Baker's sufficient condition for intertranslatability | French (2010 draft; SHPMP 2012), [LIT-170](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-170.md), read in [NOTE-162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md) from the unpaginated preprint. Every technical step is imported (Wallace, Earman, Ruetsche, Halvorson & Müger, Baker); the paper's contribution is interpretive and informal. The DHR result that statistics and charge kinds follow from the algebra is strong physics; that it favours OSR is French's reading. The modal "trans-world" structure is proposed, not developed, and the combined third option "obviously requires further elaboration". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-605](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-605.md) | In any ontological model that reproduces the quantum predictions and treats independently prepared systems as having product distributions over a joint state that is just the list of their states, distinct pure quantum states have distributions over the ontic state whose supports overlap in measure zero, so the pure state is fixed by the ontic state; approximate agreement within ε bounds the overlap by 2ε^{1/n} | Pusey, Barrett & Rudolph (2011), [LIT-062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-062.md), read in full in [NOTE-030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-030.md). For any two non-orthogonal pure states, n copies prepared independently and an entangled measurement in which each outcome is impossible for one product preparation force zero overlap; with ε error, D(µ0, µ1) ≥ 1 − 2ε^{1/n} (Eq. 7). Determinism and locality are not assumed. Preparation independence, in its strong product-space form, carries the weight, and dropping it permits ψ-epistemic models. The theorem excludes overlap, not every reading of ψ as knowledge, and it does not reach theories outside the ontological-models framework. | Active |
| [THEORY-619](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md) | Over the poset of commutative von Neumann subalgebras, coarse-graining a projector to a smaller subalgebra is exactly the direct image of its clopen region of the Gelfand spectrum under restriction, so the coarse-graining presheaf is the presheaf of clopen spectral regions; and a quantum state's sieve-valued truth values are fixed by one coherent family of regions, its supports: a proposition is true at a subcontext exactly when the support there lies under the coarse-grained proposition | Butterfield & Isham (2001), "Topos Perspective on the Kochen-Specker Theorem: IV", [LIT-382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md), read in full in [NOTE-328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-328.md). §2.4 proves G ≅ CloΣ: restricting the characters of V₁ that make P̂ true gives exactly the characters of V₂ that make its coarse-graining true, via a cited state-extension theorem. Theorem 3.1 shows that any assignment defined by "support ≤ coarse-grained proposition", with supports forming a global element of G, is a sieve-valued valuation obeying FUNC; a state's supports qualify. Both theorems are close to definitional. Nothing here builds Heyting operations on clopen sub-objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-621](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-621.md) | Indexing each quantum fact to the system it is a fact for, and computing probabilities only between facts relative to the same system, removes the contradiction between the collapse and unitary probability rules in Wigner's-friend cases; the price is that values are not held at all times or by all systems alike, there is no global view, and no quantum state of the universe | Rovelli (2021), [LIT-177](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-177.md), read in full in [NOTE-174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-174.md). For a fact a and exclusive facts bᵢ, the collapse rule Σᵢ\|W(c,bᵢ)\|²\|W(bᵢ,a)\|² and the unitary rule \|Σᵢ W(c,bᵢ)W(bᵢ,a)\|² differ by interference; RQM applies the first only when the bᵢ and c are relative to the same system. Decoherence makes some relative facts stable. The core rule is postulated, not derived, and inter-observer consistency gets one sentence. The chapter is expository, and several of its headline claims outrun its support. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-630](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-630.md) | A protective measurement yields the expectation value ⟨A⟩ on a single system in the ideal limit, and with enough observables ψ up to a global phase; this shows ψ to be ontic only if the protection procedure carries no information about ψ, a premise that Zeno and adiabatic protection, which select ψ from a discrete eigenbasis the experimenter chose, do not meet | Gao (2016), [LIT-121](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-121.md), read in full in [NOTE-140](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-140.md). Under Zeno protection the pointer shifts by exactly ⟨A⟩ with no entanglement (eqs. 1.9–1.13), and projectors on regions plus a current operator give ρ and j (eqs. 1.14–1.16). Gao argues three routes from this to ψ-ontology, claimed to need no preparation independence. All three rest on the premise that the protection does not "know" ψ, which Gao's own fn. 10 partly concedes is false. The random-discontinuous-motion ontology and the collapse model built on it are further, weaker steps. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-631.md) | Standard unitary quantum theory and the general quantum theory of open systems are intertranslatable on their common domain, so neither dependence nor justification ranks them; the open theory comes out more fundamental only through premises about interpretation, that orthodox and Everettian readings exhaust the complete readings of the state vector, and that density operators precede state vectors in how states are assigned | Cuffaro & Hartmann (2021), [LIT-037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-037.md), read in full in [NOTE-077](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-077.md). Stinespring dilation one way and dropping Lindblad terms the other make the two frameworks a tie on ontic dependence (OntFund-1) and on justification (EpFund-1). The verdict for the open theory comes from OntFund-2, which holds only if orthodox and Everettian readings are all that count, and from EpFund-2, which rests on imperfect preparation. Explanatory fundamentality is effectively abandoned. The paper proves nothing formal, and its "tout court" conclusion outruns §4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-635](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-635.md) | If the quantum state of a Bohmian system is identified with the velocity dispositions it induces on the particles, inequivalent states can share one dispositional history: every energy eigenstate of a free particle in a box induces zero velocity everywhere, so the reading erases differences of energy and of typicality unless the map from states to velocity fields is injective for generic solutions, which is conjectured, not proved | Belot (2011), [LIT-100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-100.md), read in full in [NOTE-110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md). Under the guidance law ψ(t) gives a vector field X_t on configuration space, read as a holistic disposition. For a particle in [0,1], each φn(x) = sin(πnx) gives zero velocity everywhere, so infinitely many energy eigenstates share one dispositional history, and the distinction between φ1 and φ2 in energy and typicality is lost. The rescue rests on Goldstein's unproved genericity conjecture (fn. 41), and the problem arises only for closed systems (fn. 42). It is a counterexample to one reading, not a verdict on ψ's category. | Active |
| [THEORY-656](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-656.md) | A single holistic power of the universe's configuration, carried by bare matter points, cannot ground a subsystem's effective wave function without changing the ontology, because the masses in a decoupled subsystem's Hamiltonian must belong to that subsystem's particles; dispositions intrinsic to particles or events need no such change | Dorato (2015), [LIT-176](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-176.md), read in full in [NOTE-105](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-105.md). Against Esfeld et al.'s holistic dispositionalism: when a subsystem effectively decouples, its Hamiltonian's masses must be intrinsic dispositions of its particles, so the holistic view must alter its ontology between the universal and the effective wave function (pp. 14–15). The argument is moderate and posed partly as questions. The paper's wider thesis, that events are a common primitive ontology for GRW, Bohm and ψ-antirealist views, shows compatibility only, and Dorato concedes the difference from Esfeld could be verbal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-664](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-664.md) | In a finite-dimensional probabilistic theory with unrestricted effects and local tomography, if every system can steer each of its own states from a composite with a copy of itself, every irreducible state space is homogeneous and weakly self-dual; steering does not yet give strong self-duality, so it stops short of the Jordan-algebraic and quantum state spaces | Barnum, Gaebler & Wilce (2009), [LIT-081](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-081.md), read in full in [NOTE-082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-082.md). A bipartite state steers its marginal iff its map on effects is a strong quotient of order intervals (Thm 5.4). With matching dimensions a steering state is an order-isomorphism, and a cone is homogeneous iff every interior state purifies to an isomorphism state (Thm 4.1). Hence universal self-steering gives homogeneity and weak self-duality (Prop. 5.8). The weaker Prop. 5.7 is thinly argued. The C*-algebraic conclusion of §6 needs strong self-duality, which the paper assumes rather than derives. | Active |
| [THEORY-669](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-669.md) | Reading the universal quantum state as nomological escapes the costs of reading it as a field only by paying in the theory of laws: on the strong reading, modelled on the classical Hamiltonian, a time-dependent ψ makes laws time-indexed unless the universal state is time-independent, as Wheeler–DeWitt would make it; on the weak and functionalist readings ψ need be neither unique nor time-independent, but only within an extended Humeanism whose criterion would equally make classical fields nomological | Chen (2018), [LIT-204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-204.md) ([NOTE-175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-175.md)), maps the realist readings and splits the nomological one into strong and weak. Belot (2011), [LIT-100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-100.md) ([NOTE-110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md)), ranks the costs of ψ-as-law: time-indexed laws are the serious obstacle, grades of necessity tolerable. Allori (2021), [LIT-200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-200.md) ([NOTE-154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-154.md)), makes ψ an ingredient of the law, which may be time-dependent and non-unique, and so concedes Belot's point that ψ behaves like an initial condition. Each move is an informal argument. Chen reports, without endorsing, the objection that the weak reading is too cheap, and Allori's reply embraces the case it treats as a reductio. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-687](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-687.md) | For empirically equivalent dual theories read naively, adding the common core as a candidate world does not break the underdetermination, and neither do super-empirical virtues or an overarching theory: each route to a single actual world needs a further metaphysical principle, such as the identity of indiscernibles | Le Bihan & Read (2018), [LIT-113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md), read in [NOTE-152](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-152.md) from the accepted manuscript. A nontechnical survey whose central argument is informal. It assumes a duality relates empirically equivalent models (weaker than De Haro & Butterfield's isomorphism of a bare theory), that each model is read naively and internally, and that structuralism is set aside. Its reading said it supports no existing THEORY directly; this files the conditional verdict the survey argues for, and nothing more. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-690](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-690.md) | In the physical dualities examined, theoretically inequivalent duals turn out empirically inequivalent, so dualities yield no genuine in-principle underdetermination; where duals would contradict each other a cautious realist is warranted in committing only to their common core, and because the exact cases' common cores are rich rather than empty, dualities give no support to structural realism | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A case-by-case argument over the book's examples, with a logico-semantic fallback (each dual entails the common core) for a hypothetical genuine case. The rich-core verdict is argued from exact cases (bosonization, electric–magnetic duality, T-duality) and does not reach AdS/CFT or M-theory, where structural-realist readings were proposed and the common core is "partial … ongoing work in physics!". The commitment holds only where an interpreted common core exists, which the authors say is not true in general. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-695](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-695.md) | Two quantum states can be broadcast if and only if they commute, and cloned if and only if they are identical or orthogonal; the theorem is proved for invertible density operators and marks a line within quantum theory, not a witness of nonclassicality | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), §4.3, read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md), from the Barnum–Caves–Fuchs–Jozsa–Schumacher manuscript. Fidelity cannot decrease under partial trace or under the broadcasting map, so broadcasting forces equality conditions that make ρ0 commute with the optimal-fidelity operator. Proved for invertible ρ0, ρ1 only. Spekkens' epistricted classical theories ([LIT-007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-007.md)) reproduce no-broadcasting, so the theorem states where broadcastability ends inside quantum theory and does not by itself certify nonclassicality. | Active |
| [THEORY-720](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md) | Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md), Theorems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5, read in [NOTE-651](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-651.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md), Theorems 21 and 22, read in [NOTE-647](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-647.md). A classical simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Non-contextual models are exactly those the empty model simulates, NCF cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and a model clones itself only if it is non-contextual. No-signalling models on finite scenarios only. Which maps are simulations is [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md)'s open half. | Active |
| [THEORY-721](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-721.md) | On a complex Hilbert space no orthonormal basis or tensor factorisation of given dimensions is distinguished by the space alone, and orthonormal bases correspond exactly to commutative special †-Frobenius algebras; over the reals that correspondence fails | Three results [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) rested on, held apart from its synthesis. (a) The unitary group acts transitively on the orthonormal bases of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and on its tensor factorisations of given dimensions, so neither is fixed by the space; a non-degenerate self-adjoint operator fixes a basis up to phases, and its invariant content is its spectrum. (b) Over ℂ, commutative special †-Frobenius algebras correspond exactly to orthonormal bases: Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary, [LIT-274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-274.md), Thm 5.1 and §6, in finite dimension; Abramsky & Heunen, [LIT-275](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-275.md), Thm 22, for the non-unital ones satisfying the H*-axiom, in any dimension. (c) Over ℝ it fails: ℂ as a real algebra, with multiplication scaled by 1/√2, is a commutative special †-Frobenius algebra with no nonzero copyable vector. | Active |
| [THEORY-807](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-807.md) | The guppy-type overextension in Hampton's membership data arises because a combined concept is in part a new, emergent concept and not only a logical combination of its parts, so human concept combination runs in two superposed layers, one classical and logical and one quantum and conceptual | Aerts's reading, which [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 018) to the impossibility Theorem 9 proves. Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), read in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md), fits the ∆-type deviations with one emergent subspace per pair and reads thought as two superposed layers. The narrowing was right that the theorem does not force an emergent concept, only dropping the meet or the monotone weight; this entry is the emergence reading as Aerts's thesis. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
